\begin{theorem}[Threshold degree below full parity]
\lean{FABL.isPolynomialThreshold_pred_of_ne_parityFunction_univ}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p135-b004}
\label{FABL.isPolynomialThreshold_pred_of_ne_parityFunction_univ}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.IsPolynomialThreshold, FABL.fourierCoeff, FABL.fourierCoeff_monomial, FABL.fourierCoeff_sub, FABL.fourierDegree, FABL.fourierDegree_le_iff, FABL.monomial, FABL.monomial_sq, FABL.parityFunction, FABL.parityFunction_toReal, FABL.signValue_neg_one, FABL.signValue_one, FABL.thresholdSign_of_neg, FABL.thresholdSign_of_nonneg}
\difficulty{6}
Let $n>0$ and let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$. If $f$ is neither the parity function on
all $n$ coordinates nor its negative, then $f$ has a polynomial threshold representation
of Fourier degree at most $n-1$.
\end{theorem}
